title: Periodical prompts grant the run merge authority over its docs-only notes/report PR, contradicting the dispatch review/close-out gate
description:
## As asked

Repository: JKershaw/LinearViewer (Harbour).

**Problem.** The Periodical prompts tell a run to merge its own docs-only PR, but the dispatch gate the run works under reserves merging for review and close-out. The two conflict, and runs resolve it differently.

* `lib/periodicals.js`, `areaNotes()` (\~line 313), now rendered by all 13 corrective templates after LIN-4380 (PR #2375): "Commit the report and the note edits together in one docs-only pull request … and merge it under the merge authority the second-read bullet below gives you."
* `lib/periodicals.js`, `adversarialRead()` (\~line 350), shared by all 16 templates: "This task owns merging its own report PR … merge it before the Done transition above — the report is docs-only, so merging it yourself is safe." This came from LIN-2396, which gave report PRs an owner because chains were leaving them open.
* The P1 live run (Seams & Tangles run 10, PR #2372, recorded on LIN-4349 comment `2c0a6453`) declined to merge ("merge is not mine under the dispatch") and left the merge to review and close-out. That PR still merged green, but only because a later stage merged it.

**Why it matters.** Now that all 13 corrective Periodicals write area notes through one docs-only PR, every run hits this contradiction. If a run follows the prompt, it merges past the review/close-out gate. If it follows the dispatch, the prompt's "an open report PR is not a normal terminal state" rule is broken, and LIN-2396's unmerged-report problem can come back. LIN-4382 (P4 of LIN-4349) expects "an automatic review merges its guarded notes/report PR" as its post-land witness, so it relies on whichever rule wins.

**Acceptance.**

* A recorded decision says who merges a Periodical's docs-only report/notes PR: the run itself, or review/close-out.
* The prompt text (`areaNotes()`, `adversarialRead()`) and the dispatch/close-out rules for Periodical runs agree on that decision, so no rendered prompt contradicts the gate it runs under.
* A unit test pins the agreed wording, following the style of `tests/unit/lin-3279-follow-up-shape.test.js` or the census in `tests/unit/periodicals.test.js`.
* The next live Periodical run's report PR ends merged by whoever the decision names, with no hand-off ambiguity in its closing comment.

**Priority reasoning:** medium. It affects every Periodical run from now on, and either outcome is costly (a merge past a gate, or report PRs left open). But each run so far has resolved it the safer way, and a later stage merged.

**Unvalidated idea.** This may need a ruling, not just a wording fix, because it chooses between LIN-2396's "the run owns its merge" and the dispatch's gated merge.

*End of what was asked. Steps write below this line; nothing above it changes.*

## Size of the move

**Size:** consolidate the decision this task touches
**Why:** Settles once, for all sixteen templates, who finishes a Periodical's review run: merge, Done and the closing summary; rewording only the merge lines would still send the run past the same gate at Done.
**Cuts:** none
**Decided by:** the standing policy

## Implementation Plan

Implemented as approved (plan v1, plan review `dcb96d90`), with no deviations. The ruling `lin4390-stage2-end-owner` was answered `close-out` (decision `8810f969`). The plan, research and scoping text are preserved in the task snapshots and the comment trail.

fits one session: one source file plus one comment-only file, a new test, test pin flips, a hash re-pin and one area note. Edges are listed above.
plan-review due: yes. It changes the prompt text that assigns merge and Done authority (the dispatch contract's finish line), and its last witness is live, after deploy.

## Landed

* [PR #2383](<https://github.com/JKershaw/LinearViewer/pull/2383>), merged as `f5b1f5efa25265a49cb3c6ca04879610fcc278f9` and deployed 2026-11-10.
* All 16 Periodical templates now hand off: the run leaves a green, rebased docs-only PR plus its PR-URL, second-read and closing comments. Review approves; close-out merges, sets Done and posts the summary. `conclude()`/`concludeAdvisory()` were renamed `handOff()`/`handOffAdvisory()`. The new `tests/unit/lin-4390-periodical-hand-off.test.js` reads both the prompt side and the gate side across 32 renders.
* The live witness (acceptance 4) was not run at close-out: no dispatch grant. See the close-out comment for the check and who can run it.
* Full history: task snapshots and the comment trail.

comments.body:
## Survey open-0: LIN-4390 @ b315e0e8f

**The merge clash is a symptom.** The Stage-2 text in `lib/periodicals.js` still describes one session that finishes its own work. The header comment (~l.85: "SELF-CONCLUDES … one docs-only PR it merges itself"), `conclude()` (l.322–326: "move the task to its done/completed state") and `adversarialRead()` (l.350: "merge it before the Done transition") all say so. But Stage-2 now runs as an ordinary task through implement → review → close-out (LIN-1279, LIN-2575; `lib/periodical-runs.js:237` assumes "a Periodical's own PR merges after its Stage-2 row was dispatched"). The gate gives **Done** to close-out as well as merge (`lib/prompt-template-defs.js:986`, `:1024`; `lib/proxy-preamble.js:424`). If only the merge sentences change, `conclude()` still tells the run to set Done past that same gate. The ruling has to cover the run's whole end state (merge, Done and closing comment), not just who merges.

**Why it will be hard:**
- **No gate is in code.** Nothing refuses a session's merge. The "Approve + ledger" gate is prose in four places (preamble, kickoff l.440/466, review, close-out). `lib/periodical-report-gate.js` checks Done for an evidence URL and the second-read comment, never merges. So "agree" means prose agreeing with prose: the unit test can only pin wording, and the live run is the only real witness.
- **Tests pin the current words:** `tests/unit/periodicals.test.js:233-234` ("owns merging its own report PR", "merge it before the Done transition") and l.1387 ("merge authority"). `adversarialRead` is shared by all 16 templates, and the 3 advisory ones open no notes PR, so the `notes` branch needs care.
- **The second-read order changes.** If close-out sets Done, the run has to post the comment before it hands off, or close-out's Done write fails `hasAdversarialReadEvidenceComment`.
- **LIN-4382's witness names the wrong stage.** It says "an automatic review merges …", but review never merges; close-out does. Fix that wording too.
- **LIN-2396's risk only exists off the chain.** Check whether any entrance (plain Mint, direct `/dispatch`) runs a Stage-2 task with no close-out after it. On that path, a green docs PR stays open again.

**What I'd do first:** record the ruling on this ticket before editing anything. I recommend **close-out merges and sets Done**. The run stops at a green, rebased docs-only PR plus the second-read comment, and its closing comment names close-out as next. That matches every existing gate and what the P1 run did (PR #2372). LIN-2396's "an open PR is not terminal" rule then becomes close-out's job. Then rewrite `areaNotes()`, `adversarialRead()`, `conclude()` and the header together in one change. Update the tests so they pin the hand-off and fail if "merges itself", "owns merging" or "move the task to its done" comes back.

## Survey global: LIN-4390 @ b315e0e8f

**Where it lands.** `lib/periodicals.js` (llm-and-prompts area). It's getting tidier: LIN-4379/4380 moved 13 templates onto shared bullets, so one wording change reaches every run. The gate it conflicts with is prose in four other places: `lib/proxy-preamble.js:424` ("merge and Done are gated separately on a recorded review Approve…"), `lib/prompts/autopilot-kickoff.js:440,466` ("never merge"), review's "You do NOT merge, mark the task Done" (`lib/prompt-template-defs.js:986`), and close-out's merge → Done → summary (`:1022–1058`). The only gate in code is `lib/periodical-report-gate.js`. It checks evidence and the adversarial-read comment before Done, not who merged or whether review approved.

**The ticket is aimed at a symptom.** Merge is one of three self-finish instructions. `conclude()` also tells the run to "move the task to its done/completed state" and says the job ends "once the report and the note edits are merged". The header (`:84–99`, "it merges itself", "closes itself") repeats the same contract. That contract (LIN-386's "self-conclude") predates Stage-2 runs going through autopilot. Mint + Autopilot now hands the minted task to a scoped autopilot run, which follows the normal stages, so the run gets a prompt older than the pipeline it runs in. If only the merge wording changes, `conclude()` still sends the run past the same gate at the Done transition.

**Done the obvious way** (reword the two bullets and flip `tests/unit/periodicals.test.js:233–236,1387`): cheap, but leaves the header and `conclude()` out of step. It also leaves "an open report PR is not a normal terminal state" with no owner. If the ruling is instead "the run merges", that becomes a second, Periodical-only merge rule beside close-out's. No code knows a docs-only lane. And "docs-only, so safe" isn't quite true now: area notes are prompt input that scoping and every later change read. `docs/steady-base.md:84` records review catching real faults in docs-only changes, served prompt text among them.

**What has to learn about it:** the header, `conclude()`, the tests above, LIN-4382's witness wording, and the llm-and-prompts area note. No test reads both the Periodical text and the gate prose, so nothing would notice drift.

**Better, at a cost this task can carry:** rule once that close-out merges and sets Done, the dispatch rule. Then change the Stage-2 contract so its end state is "report + notes PR open and green, adversarial-read comment posted, hand off to review". Remove merge and Done from `areaNotes`, `adversarialRead` and `conclude`, and rewrite the header to match. Add one test that renders all 16 templates and asserts that none tells the run to merge or set Done. LIN-2396's concern keeps a home: close-out owns "see it land".

**Better still, not this task's:** gate authority lives as prose in five or more places with no single source. A shared leaf constant, like `lib/prompts/leftover-words.js` or `autopilot-precedence.js`, imported by the preamble, kickoff, review, close-out and Periodicals, would stop this from happening again. So would a server check on who merges. Both are wider than this ticket.

## Decision (autopilot, recorded): close-out finishes a Periodical review run

**Decision.** Close-out merges a Periodical's docs-only report/notes PR, sets Done and posts the final summary. The Periodical run itself stops at a green, rebased PR plus the second-read comment, and its closing comment names close-out as next. This answers option `close-out` of scoping's question `lin4390-stage2-end-owner`.

**Why (engineering, so settled here, not escalated).** (1) It matches the dispatch gate every other stage already runs under: review authorizes, close-out merges and sets Done. `run-self` would add a second merge rule that applies only to Periodicals. (2) It is the conservative direction: it grants no new merge authority, so nothing needs John's sign-off. (3) It matches what the live P1 run did (PR #2372) and what LIN-4382's witness ("an automatic review merges its guarded notes/report PR") needs, with the actor named as close-out. (4) LIN-2396's concern that an open report PR is not a normal terminal state is kept by making close-out own that PR; the run's own terminal state is deliberately open-and-green with a named hand-off.

**Scope for implementation.** Reword `areaNotes()`, `adversarialRead()`, `conclude()` and the header comment in `lib/periodicals.js` together. Add a unit test that renders all 16 templates and fails if any tells the run to merge or set Done itself. Re-measure `tests/unit/prompt-size-budget.test.js` ceilings. Make the dispatch/close-out rules for Periodical runs agree (close-out owns the merge). A shared constant or a server-side who-merged check is out of scope; note it as a follow-up only if outside the bounded class.

Plan v1 written into the description (`## Implementation Plan`, grounded at `b315e0e8f`). It follows the recorded decision (`8810f969`): close-out merges and sets Done, and the run hands off at a green, rebased PR with its evidence and second-read comments posted. The change goes in the shared bullets (`areaNotes`, `conclude`, `concludeAdvisory`, `adversarialRead`) and the header. The gate prose stays as is; a new test reads both sides across all 32 renders. The brief's open question (off-chain runs) is answered in the plan: no Periodical-specific hole. No open minted task carries the old wording. fits one session · plan-review due: yes.

### Plan Review Verdict

**Verdict:** Approve — the plan fixes the cause (Stage-2's self-finish contract, covering merge *and* Done), not just the two merge sentences, and every fact it rests on holds at `b315e0e8f` (origin/main has not moved since).

**How it meets what was asked:** "A recorded decision says who merges" → `8810f969` (close-out). "The prompt text (`areaNotes()`, `adversarialRead()`) and the dispatch/close-out rules … agree" → shared bullets plus header rewritten; gate prose already says close-out, so it stays as it is, and a test reads both sides. "A unit test pins the agreed wording" → new `lin-4390-periodical-hand-off.test.js` plus flipped census asserts. "The next live Periodical run's report PR ends merged by whoever the decision names" → post-deploy witness, owned by close-out. Nothing is narrowed: widening the scope to `conclude()`/`concludeAdvisory()`/header follows from the cause. Acceptance 4 is deferred until after deploy, not cut.

**What I checked**
- **The premise holds.** `lib/periodicals.js:313` (`areaNotes` "merge it under the merge authority…"), `:323-329` (`conclude`/`concludeAdvisory` "move the task to its done/completed state"), `:350` (`adversarialRead` "owns merging … docs-only, so merging it yourself is safe") and header `:84-115` ("SELF-CONCLUDES … closes itself", "PR it merges itself", "self-close contract") all say what the plan says. On the gate side: `lib/proxy-preamble.js:424`, review "You do NOT merge, mark the task Done" and close-out "Merge pinned … Then set the task to Done" in `lib/prompt-template-defs.js`, and the kickoff's finish line all give merge and Done to close-out. Fixing only the merge lines would leave `conclude()` setting Done past the gate. The plan is right about that.
- **The fix reaches all 16 templates.** `adversarialRead` is appended to every template by `buildPeriodicalScaffold` (`:252`). `areaNotes` and `conclude` appear 13× each, and `concludeAdvisory` 3× (`:560`, `:640`, `:823`). These match the mutation counts the plan gives (13/13/3/16).
- **The places list is complete.** I re-ran the plan's grep, widened to `self-close|Done transition|report PR` and `public/`. The only hits outside the listed places are generic close-out text in `prompt-template-defs.js`/`prompt-templates.test.js`, which is about close-out's own Done and is correct, plus historical docs (`docs/lin-370-research-notes.md`, `docs/collective-session-2026-06-12.md`, `docs/v1.md`). Those docs are the same historical-record kind as the excluded `docs/reviews/`, and `docs/v1.md` already says close-out merges. The scaffold's mint closing (`:246`, "before this task can be marked done") is neutral and needs no change.
- **The safeguards hold.** The change only takes authority away; it grants none. The Done gate (`lib/periodical-report-gate.js`) is untouched and now fires on close-out's write. The plan correctly makes the evidence-URL and second-read comments come *before* the hand-off, so close-out's Done is not refused. LIN-2396's failure (Done with the PR open) cannot recur, because only close-out writes Done and it merges first.
- **The tests it names exist and do what it says.** `lin-4313-periodical-prompt-bytes.test.js` pins 16 × {plain, autopilot} = 32 hashes, with a header paragraph for each re-pin (LIN-4353 and LIN-4380 precedents). `prompt-size-budget.test.js` measures no Periodical prompt, only stage templates (e.g. scoping). The style reference `lin-3279-follow-up-shape.test.js` exists.

**Notes for the builder (none blocking)**
1. **Area-note cap headroom is 71 bytes.** `docs/areas/llm-and-prompts.md` is 6,073 B against `NOTE_BYTE_CAP = 6144` (`tests/unit/area-notes.test.js:19`). The new Lesson will not fit unless you prune or distil an existing entry in the same edit. Plan for that rather than discovering it from the cap test.
2. **Witness (a) needs precise matching.** "Any run-directed 'merge it'" will false-positive on the new hand-off text ("close-out merges it"). Match the retired phrases exactly (`owns merging`, `merge it before the Done`, `merge it under the merge authority`, `move the task to its done`, `merging it yourself is safe`, `self-conclud`). Add a narrow imperative pattern only if it stays clear of close-out-subject sentences. Then do the mutation check per bullet, as the plan says.
3. **Keep the second-read bullet's title consistent.** "Get a fresh-context adversarial second-read before this task can conclude" will still read correctly if "conclude" now means the hand-off. But the body's "AGREE and DISAGREE both conclude this task normally" and "never blocks concluding" are pinned at `tests/unit/periodicals.test.js:230`. Decide whether "conclude" now means hand-off, say so once in the bullet, and flip that assert if the words change.
4. **Close-out's Follow-up Triage vs "never to a ticket".** Close-out files review's *outside* ledger items as tickets. For a Periodical PR, that is a different source from the run's findings, so there is no conflict. Still, the hand-off sentence should not suggest that close-out carries the run's findings into tickets. Findings still go only to notes and the closing comment.
5. **External writes: check before you post.** Before posting the correction comments on LIN-4382 and LIN-4349, and before minting a witness lane, check whether either already exists (the brief's open questions). On LIN-4382, cite the exact witness line "an automatic review merges its guarded notes/report PR" and leave its `## As asked` untouched.
6. **Optional, in the same pass:** the `lib/periodicals.js` header's "Concluding is the point: a review task left In Progress is re-recommended … forever (LIN-386)" should become the new reason. Staying In Progress until close-out is now the *intended* path back through review → close-out, not a failure.

On Approve: to `implementation` with the notes above.

Close-out does all three; the run stops at a green, rebased PR plus the second-read comment, then hands off to review

— Ruling recorded via Harbour

## Implementation — LIN-4390

**PR:** https://github.com/JKershaw/LinearViewer/pull/2383 (head `a9fe77936`, branch `feat/lin-4390-periodical-hand-off`). **CI: all 7 checks pass** (`CI success`, Unit tests, E2E 1–4/4, Secret scan).

**What changed (decision `8810f969`, plan v1):** all 16 Periodical templates now end at a hand-off. The run gets its PR rebased and green, posts the PR's URL as soon as it is open, gets the second read, then posts a closing comment naming review as approver and close-out as the stage that merges, sets Done and posts the final summary. The run never merges and never sets Done, and the task stays In Progress until close-out finishes.
- `lib/periodicals.js`: rewrote `areaNotes`, `conclude` and `concludeAdvisory` (now one shared `handOffBullet`), `adversarialRead` and the header contract. Kept the AGREE/DISAGREE semantics, "if it opened one" and the named-blocker escape (now: the PR cannot be made green). The 3 advisory templates gain no area-notes PR.
- `lib/periodical-report-gate.js`: header comment only. No logic or message change.
- Gate prose (preamble, kickoff, review, close-out) is unchanged, as planned. The new test pins it.

**Builder decisions, with reasons:**
- "Conclude" is defined as the hand-off by renaming, not by a gloss (plan-review note 3). The bullet titles read "Then hand off…" and "…second-read before you hand off". "AGREE and DISAGREE both conclude this task normally" became "…both end in the normal hand-off".
- "never a reason to leave this task open pending a human" became "…hold back the hand-off pending a human". The task now *is* left open until close-out, so the old words would have contradicted the new contract.
- The evidence-link comment is ordered first: "As soon as the area-notes pull request is open, post its full URL…" comes before the second read and the closing comment, so close-out's Done isn't refused (likeliest-break #1).

**Witnesses:**
- New `tests/unit/lin-4390-periodical-hand-off.test.js` covers 32 renders plus 3 gate-side pins (close-out, review, preamble).
  - Fails before: with HEAD's `lib/periodicals.js`, all 16 templates fail (32/36 tests fail).
  - Mutation, one bullet restored at a time: `areaNotes` fails 13 templates, `conclude` 13, `concludeAdvisory` 3, `adversarialRead` 16, matching the plan. Breaking the close-out, review or preamble wording fails each gate pin.
- `lin-4313` prompt bytes: all 32 hashes re-pinned, with a LIN-4390 header paragraph. With the 4 old bullets swapped back in, the old hashes pass, so those bullets are the only change.
- The census in `periodicals.test.js` is flipped to the hand-off. `prompt-size-budget` is untouched and passes (it measures no Periodical). `area-notes`, both report-gate suites, `lin-3279`, `periodical-runs` and `workspace-features` pass.
- Full local `npm run test:unit`: 24,734/24,735. The single failure, `scripts/code-shape/wrappers.test.mjs` "without acorn…", fails identically on `main` here and passes in CI.
- Stale-wording grep over lib/routes/tests/public/scripts/docs (excluding historical records) comes back clean.

**Area notes** (`docs/areas/llm-and-prompts.md`): added the Lesson. Following plan-review note 1, I distilled four existing entries in the same edit, and the note now sits at exactly 6,144 B, the cap. I pruned the no-longer-true clause "nothing uses it yet" from the `lib/should-mock-ai.js` entry: `lib/dispatch-entrance.js` and `lib/dispatch-factory.js` now use `isHermeticTestToken`. Binding lessons followed: the frozen prompt size (measured, no ceiling moved), and "prompt words that ban a kind of how do not hold it", which is why every render is held by a test.

**Open questions from the brief, checked:**
- Correction comments on LIN-4382 / LIN-4349: **none posted yet**. Their LIN-4390 mentions only list it as an outside follow-up. Close-out owns these after merge: quote "an automatic review merges its guarded notes/report PR" and name close-out as the actor, leaving LIN-4382's `## As asked` untouched.
- Post-deploy witness lane: none minted or run for this. **Still to run after deploy (close-out):** the next live Periodical run hands off explicitly; its PR is merged by a close-out session after that session's dispatch; the summary cites the merge commit; Done is set only after the merge. Context: on 8 Nov a Design & Interface run (LIN-4391) "merged and set Done itself" (LIN-4349 comment, 16:04 UTC), which is the behaviour this removes.

Cuts to the As-asked block: none. I did not merge; that is for review, then close-out.

### Leftovers

PR: https://github.com/JKershaw/LinearViewer/pull/2383 · head `5f2248de8f72e7416063802c31777e0674da57c1` · CI: all 7 checks pass (CI success, Unit tests, E2E 1–4/4, Secret scan).

- **A name my change made untrue:** `conclude()` / `concludeAdvisory()` in `lib/periodicals.js` were named for LIN-386's self-concluding run → **tidied**: renamed `handOff()` / `handOffAdvisory()` (16 call sites). The rendered bytes don't change; all 32 `lin-4313` hashes still match.
- **A comment my change made untrue:** `lib/periodical-report-gate.js` described the second read as coming "before concluding" → **tidied**: now "before handing off (LIN-4390)". Test comments follow the rename.
- **One rule spelled in many places:** who merges and sets Done is retyped in three Periodical bullets (`handOffBullet`, `areaNotes`, `adversarialRead`) and four gate texts (review and close-out in `lib/prompt-template-defs.js`, `lib/prompts/autopilot-kickoff.js`, `lib/proxy-preamble.js`). Only `lin-4390-periodical-hand-off` links them → **noted**: a `## Waiting` entry in `docs/areas/llm-and-prompts.md`. A shared leaf constant is bigger than fix-sized, and the decision put it out of this ticket's scope.
- **Lesson** for the next builder (`docs/areas/llm-and-prompts.md`): close-out merges a Periodical's PR and sets Done, as for any task; give no Periodical its own merge rule, because notes are prompt input.
- **Waiting entries settled or made untrue:** none. Main's Drift & Coherence run 6 (#2385) had already reworded the `isHermeticTestToken` entry, so I kept main's wording when merging. I distilled the note's existing entries without dropping any facts so it fits the cap (6,142 of 6,144 B).
- **Merged origin/main** (`1e106e4e3`) into the branch. The only conflict was in the area note; main's changes since my branch were docs only.
- **For close-out:** nothing new. Already listed on the build comment: the correction comments on LIN-4382 / LIN-4349 and the post-deploy live check.

## Review — LIN-4390

Reviewed [PR #2383](https://github.com/JKershaw/LinearViewer/pull/2383) at head `5f2248de8f72e7416063802c31777e0674da57c1` (branch `feat/lin-4390-periodical-hand-off`). The PR is open and mergeable, and origin/main has not moved since the branch merged it (`139caf95d`).

CI: green. All 7 checks pass on `5f2248de8`: CI success, Unit tests, E2E 1–4/4, Secret scan.

### Scope against the plan
The diff touches six files, the same places as plan v1 (places 1–8). Place 9, the correction comments on LIN-4382 and LIN-4349, is close-out's job by design. Nothing overran the plan. The gate prose in `lib/proxy-preamble.js`, `lib/prompts/autopilot-kickoff.js` and review/close-out in `lib/prompt-template-defs.js` is unchanged, as planned. The `lib/periodical-report-gate.js` change is comments only, with no logic or message change. The ruling `lin4390-stage2-end-owner` is answered as `close-out` (comment `797c0bc5`, decision `8810f969`).

### What I checked myself
- **Rendered text.** I rendered the corrective and advisory templates and read them. `areaNotes` now ends "review approves it and close-out merges it, never this run". `handOffBullet` puts the PR-link comment first, then the second read, then a closing comment that names review and close-out, with "neither merges nor moves the task to Done". `adversarialRead` keeps "if it opened one", AGREE/DISAGREE (now "end in the normal hand-off"), the named-blocker escape (the PR cannot be made green) and "an open … report pull request is not a normal terminal state", which now explains why the task stays In Progress until close-out merges. The 3 advisory templates gain no area-notes wording. `PERIODICAL_AUTOPILOT_TAIL` says nothing about merge or Done, so it does not conflict.
- **Targeted suites at head, all green:** `lin-4390-periodical-hand-off` (36), `lin-4313-periodical-prompt-bytes` (2), `periodicals` (492), `area-notes` (7), `periodical-report-gate` (31), `proxy-periodical-report-gate-route` (8), `prompt-size-budget` (17), `lin-3279-follow-up-shape` (5), `periodical-runs` (79).
- **Mutation checks (LIN-2274),** each reverted afterwards with a clean tree confirmed:
  - `areaNotes` put back to "merge it under the merge authority…": 13 template tests fail × 2 variants = 26.
  - `handOffBullet` "neither merges nor moves the task to Done" changed to "move the task to its done/completed state": 32 fail (all 16 × 2).
  - `adversarialRead` put back to "owns merging its own report PR: merge it before the Done transition": 32 fail.
  - `handOffAdvisory` closeOut set to "may merge": 6 fail (the 3 advisory × 2).
  - Gate side: in `lib/prompt-template-defs.js`, close-out's "Then set the task to Done." changed to something else: the close-out pin fails.
  
  So the tests pin the claimed behaviour on both sides.
- **Regression check:** I ran `git log` on all five touched source and test files. The recent LIN-4379/4380/4381 commits shaped these bullets, and their behaviour still holds: no Periodical mints a follow-up, the census of filing words passes, and `notes` is switched only where the wording differs. Nothing reverted is re-applied.
